newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LATE BIRDIE SPREE GIVES PRICE FIRST-ROUND HERITAGE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LATE BIRDIE SPREE GIVES PRICE FIRST-ROUND HERITAGE LEAD.

text.p: Nick Price of Zimbabwe rode a hot finish to the top of the leaderboard and a one-stroke lead after the first round of the Heritage Classic golf tournament on Thursday.
Price recovered from a poor start with birdies on his final five holes to card a six-under-par 65 -- a rather remarkable score in strong afternoon winds at the tight Harbour Town course.
Rick Fehr, Tom Watson and Brad Faxon were tied for second place, one stroke behind Price with Lennie Clements and Hal Sutton another stroke back at 67.
Fehr got to seven under before double-bogeying the final hole to drop back into a tie for second.
Price, winner of three major championships, began his round at the 10th and promptly bogeyed his first two holes, three-putting both times.

"Sometimes you get a little wild when that happens. I was just fine," he said. "I have been hitting the ball really well and I felt that if I just kept my head together, especially on a windy day like today, that I was going to make some birdies.
"I have been playing well since September, October of last year, and today I just put it all together. It is a lot of fun when you do that, especially on a tough day like today."

After his rough start, Price picked up two birdies to make the turn at level par. He then birdied the first hole and parred the next three before stringing together five birdies from inside 20 feet to close out his round.

Price, 39, has shown signs this year of the form that took him to the world's top ranking only two years ago. He won twice on the South African Tour in February, and stands a 16th on the PGA Tour money list after playing just five events.
Meanwhile, Britain's Colin Montgomerie shot an even-par 71, then promptly denied reports he was likely to join the U.S. PGA Tour next year.
"I'm a European Tour player and I enjoy playing over here," said Montgomerie, the European tour's top money winner the past four years.
He said he would make a decision later this year, but the speculation is that he will play most of his golf in the United States next year, while remaining a European Tour member.

Montgomerie, playing for the sixth time in the past seven weeks on the U.S. PGA Tour, likes the practice facilities in the United States and believes the unsurpassed level of competition would be good for his game.
